payload.markdown: This chapter covered a lot of ground, taking a class from an empty implementation through to a fully featured inheritance hierarchy. You took in some design issues, particularly with regard to type and inheritance. You saw PHP’s support for visibility and explored some of its uses. In the next chapter, I will show you more of PHP’s object-oriented features.

items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Inheritance: Deriving a class from a base class to reuse and specialise its behaviour.
Visibility & Encapsulation: public, protected and private control who may read or write a member.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
